records.title: Dynamic DNN Model Switching for Collaborative Edge Intelligence in UAV Swarm
records.venue: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)

primary_full_report.rationale: Full 7-page IEEE WCSP 2023 conference paper presenting a system model, accuracy-latency utility optimization, genetic-algorithm-based Dynamic Model Switching (DMS) algorithm, and trace-driven simulations.
primary_full_report.quote: Based on genetic algorithms, we then propose an efficient algorithm called Dynamic Model Switching (DMS) that can output the best DNN model switching policy according to the current UAV communication environment.

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Models N heterogeneous UAVs with time-varying links and evaluates swarms of 4 to 8 UAVs (5 UAVs in Fig. 2 and Table 1) using real-world Mid-Air trajectory traces.
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: To provide a clearer comparison of the performance of the five algorithms, we have created Table. 1, which displays the latency and accuracy for a swarm of five UAVs under seven inference request scenario.

collaborative_inference.rationale: Dynamically switches each request between single-UAV execution of a lightweight CNN (AlexNet/SqueezeNet) and multi-UAV layer-partitioned execution of a large CNN (VGG16) across swarm UAVs.
collaborative_inference.quote: In collaborative inference, large complex model needs to be partitioned and executed on different UAVs.

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Evaluates VGG16 paired with AlexNet and SqueezeNet in Mid-Air trace-driven simulations using embedded hardware parameters against GA-uniform, GA-random, Small-only, and Large-only baselines.
evaluative_evidence.quote: In our study, we employ VGG16 as the large complex model, while for the small lightweight model, we utilize both AlexNet and SqueezeNet.

date_window.rationale: Published in 2023 IEEE WCSP proceedings (2023 copyright), within 2021-01-01 through 2026-11-25.
date_window.quote: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)

english.rationale: Full 7-page conference paper is written in English.
english.quote: Deploying machine learning (ML) algorithms on Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarm to perform real-time tasks such as object detection is currently a hot research topic.

alignment.rationale: Core dynamic orchestration of model switching between single-UAV lightweight CNN inference and multi-UAV partitioned large CNN inference under time-varying inter-UAV links.
alignment.quote: By dynamically switching between these two models, we have developed an efficient DNN model execution policy that achieves both low latency and high accuracy.

records.title: A hybrid fast inference approach with distributed neural networks for edge computing enabled UAV swarm

primary_full_report.rationale: Full-length 12-page peer-reviewed Elsevier Physical Communication journal article presenting a distributed early-exit DNN framework, optimization problem, heuristic policies, and simulations.
primary_full_report.quote: Considering image processing in UAV applications, we propose a hybrid inference framework combining early exit and task offloading based on distributed neural network.

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Evaluates a two-tier multi-UAV architecture of 12 drone terminals wirelessly connected to 4 laser-linked aerial computing centers serving as edge servers.
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: The simulation scenario includes 4 edge servers with 12 drone terminals. The computing capacity of local users is 4.8 GHz, and the computing capacity of edge devices is 52 GHz.

collaborative_inference.rationale: Splits a 32-layer Branchy/ResNet DNN into a 10-layer bottlenecked early-exit head on drone terminals and a 22-layer tail on aerial edge servers, orchestrating local early exit, compressed feature upload, raw offloading, and inter-server load balancing.
collaborative_inference.quote: We design one early exit at the shallow level, deploy the shallow network at the drone terminals, and the entire network at the edge servers.

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Trains the Branchy/ResNet model in PyTorch on CIFAR-10 and runs 5000-cycle multi-UAV simulations evaluating PLUTU and PLPTU against AL, AO, and RS across radio resources, task generation rates, and drone computing capacities.
evaluative_evidence.quote: We train our model with the CIFAR data set, in which each image contains 32*32 RGB pixels. We use Pytorch as our deep learning framework to build our DNN experimentation platform.

date_window.rationale: Available online 24 June 2023 in Physical Communication Vol. 60, within 2021-01-01 through 2026-11-25.

english.rationale: Full 12-page journal article is written in English.
english.quote: The proposed approach efficiently utilizes wireless transmission and balances the computation load to maximize the system inference accuracy within the latency constraints.

alignment.rationale: Core orchestration of hybrid early-exit local inference, bottlenecked split-DNN intermediate feature uploading, direct raw offloading, and adjacent aerial-server queue balancing across a 12-drone, 4-aerial-server swarm.
alignment.quote: In the proposed framework, we focus on three sections to take effective actions that maximize the system inference accuracy.
